Hi team / Claire —

Quick responses and an action plan. Answers below are high-level; we will populate the questionnaire fields and attach artifacts by EOD tomorrow (18 Feb) per procurement’s deadline.

1) SOC 2 scope: Our 2025 Type II report covers hosted inference (API endpoints), data plane services, and operational controls around key custody for Redwood-managed keys. We will include a short statement clarifying that Redwood-managed KMS controls referenced in the report apply to the inference service. See attached redwood-soc2-summary-2025-12.pdf for details.

2) HIPAA / BAA: Redwood supports HIPAA-covered workloads on our Dedicated and Private deployment options today. For hosted customers processing PHI, we can execute a BAA; legal has a standard BAA template. For AlphaMed’s use case we recommend Dedicated or Private if they require strict separation, but we can provide controls and a BAA for hosted with CMK. Action: I’ll loop Legal and attach the BAA template.

3) CMK/BYOK options (recommended approach):
- Option A (recommended for HIPAA): Customer-managed keys via their cloud KMS (we integrate with GCP KMS / AWS KMS) — keys never leave their KMS; Redwood performs cryptographic operations via API calls with strong delegation and access controls.
- Option B: BYOK into Redwood-managed HSM (FIPS 140-2/3 compliant) with dual-control (customer roles + Redwood operator roles). Good when customer cannot grant cross-account KMS access.
- Option C: Redwood-managed keys (fastest, lowest-friction) — still HSM-backed by our provider.

4) Encryption controls (summary for auditors):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ (1.3 preferred), TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 or stronger; mutual TLS available for Private deployments.
- At-rest: All inference ephemeral caches and persistent model artifacts are AES-256 encrypted; disk encryption via provider-managed encrypted volumes; DBs use encryption-at-rest and column-level protections for tokens/keys (where applicable).
- Key management: HSM-backed master keys for root of trust; per-customer key wrapping and access policies; logs and KMS audit trails retained per SLA.

Action items / next steps:
- Rishi: populate questionnaire answers and attach SOC2 summary + BAA template by EOD 18 Feb.
- Monica: if AlphaMed prefers a technical run-through, I recommend a 45-min design session to map key flow (we can include diagrams).
- Priyom: propose a 30–45 min slot; I’ve included a tentative calendar link: https://calendar.redwood.ai/pri-y/30min?cid=alphamed-call

Claire — happy to jump on a technical call. Which option above sounds closest to what your security team expects? We’ll tailor the questionnaire responses accordingly.

Thanks —
